blocks.title: Separate control plane
blocks.text: Implement issue automation as a GitHub App control plane outside the CloudX workstation-control server and web runtime. The manager owns durable state and dispatch, but it never executes repository code, receives a model credential, publishes a candidate, or mounts a Docker socket.

Phase supplies the useful fresh-role and adversarial-review pattern. CloudX extends it with authenticated issue intake, immutable context, durable CAS state, bounded capacity, isolated generation, static policy-selected review, separate publication credentials, repository protection, and exact post-merge proof.

The current CloudX controller is Phase-inspired, not behaviorally identical. One immutable issue revision receives one privileged workflow attempt and one bounded synthesis-review sequence. A finding or changed requirement returns to a new canonical issue revision and run instead of granting an agent an open-ended model repair loop.

claims.text: The AI manager is an independent durable control plane, not a capability inside the CloudX product runtime or an execution worker.

evidence.excerpt: The manager is a separate non-root read-only and resource-bounded container with resource-bounded PostgreSQL and artifact storage, not a service inside apps/server.
Composition includes GitHub intake, durable lifecycle, projection, and callback services but no model client, repository executor, or Docker client.

claims.text: CloudX retains Phase-style independent role review while adding durable unattended issue-to-PR and exact-merge authorities that Phase's contributor skill does not provide.

blocks.text: Every mutation boundary receives the narrowest credential for its deterministic task. Each serialized model job runs as the non-root cloudx-codex account on one dedicated private self-hosted runner and invokes the pinned CLI with persistent file-backed ChatGPT authentication. Exact audited profiles expose minimal runtime paths, temporary files, and workspace read access; only bounded reproduction receives workspace write authority. Implementation synthesis has no shell tool and emits a proposal without trusted byte or digest claims. Trusted code captures the exact patch, and only the credential-free no-network verifier applies or executes it. Every verifier and Git command has an explicit timeout and stdout/stderr ceiling. POSIX execution owns a detached process group, sends TERM then bounded KILL, rejects residual descendants, and waits for cleanup before hashing the worktree. GitHub publication and main update use separate Apps and never execute candidate code.

claims.text: Durable lifecycle, model judgment, candidate execution, candidate publication, review publication, human authorization, and main update remain separate authorities.

evidence.excerpt: Every model job uses the exact dedicated runner and local logged-in Codex action; implementation synthesis disables shell_tool, verification is credential-free, and publisher credentials appear only after validation.
Area and aggregate reviewers are read-only; the trusted publish job validates artifacts before publishing a check.
Manager, Candidate Publisher, and Merge Authority Apps have distinct slugs and exact permission sets.

blocks.text: Ingress verifies the exact webhook bytes and delivery headers before durable insertion. A worker then discards unsupported events, ignores manager-authored feedback loops, and recaptures only issue-author or repository-writer comment changes. Pushes to main invalidate stale generation bases and initiate recapture.

Canonical capture reads current issue metadata, calculated repository permission for every bounded issue actor, the authoritative author-or-writer comments and timeline, repository privacy, current main SHA, and the policy bytes. Author association is descriptive only: read and triage users, drive-by users, and manager-authored comments are excluded from the model-visible snapshot, semantic revision, and media set. Admitted media downloads are bounded by host, HTTPS shape, redirects, time, count, bytes, declared MIME, and detected file type. Source revision schema v2 binds each accepted source URL to the downloaded SHA-256, MIME type, and byte count. A second issue read must reproduce authority and the URL-level issue document revision around that download; the persisted source revision is then computed from the downloaded descriptors. Merge authorization repeats both issue reads and bounded media downloads and requires the same v2 source revision before consuming the one-time capability.

blocks.title: Writer authority and private media
blocks.text: A current write, maintain, or admin author is admitted directly. Another reporter requires ai:issue-approved from a current writer, and that label event must be strictly newer than the latest authoritative issue edit or comment update. Equal or stale timestamps fail closed. Private attachment intake fails explicitly.

claims.text: Only an HMAC-authenticated, current-writer-authorized, double-read canonical issue revision can consume generation capacity; source revision v2 binds accepted media bytes and is recomputed before merge, and media intake is bounded and public-only.

evidence.excerpt: Delivery identity and event syntax are validated and the raw body HMAC is checked before persistence.
Two canonical issue document reads surround bounded downloads. Source revision schema v2 binds each retained media URL to its downloaded SHA-256, MIME type, and byte count.

Calculated write, maintain, or admin permission authorizes an actor; member or collaborator association alone does not. External-author approval must post strictly after the latest authoritative revision.
Only bounded HTTPS GitHub attachment hosts, paths, redirects, byte counts, MIME types, and detected bytes are accepted.

Tests cover signature order, canonical mutation, same-URL byte changes, merge-time media reauthorization, authority filtering, quotas, redirect confinement, MIME mismatch, and private attachment rejection.
Merge authorization rereads the canonical issue around bounded media downloads and requires the resulting v2 revision to equal the stored run revision before capability consumption.

items: An authoritative issue edit, comment edit, approval change, media change, or current-main change supersedes evidence tied to the old source revision or base.
A managed PR head change supersedes the run. A close without merge cancels it. A Merge Authority App close event can still reconcile a merge that raced workflow completion.
A terminal managed result cannot arrive before all eight durable stage rows, exact artifact digests, and correct base-versus-candidate head bindings exist.
Snapshot, media, and stage writes reserve bounded logical capacity before publication; no-overwrite receipts and reference-checked cleanup prevent failed writes from deleting shared evidence.

Active capacity is keyed by run. A new canonical revision excludes the same issue's replaceable managed-run slot so it can reach supersession, but processing, registration-ambiguous, and dispatched workflows still retain their external-execution lease. Saturation persists the replacement as a non-active blocked admission and cannot dispatch another workflow.

Terminal raw snapshots, media references, and stage bytes compact after retention, while run events, result identity, stage digests, subject digests, sizes, compaction timestamps, and explicit operator resolutions remain auditable.

Raw delivery identity remains for the configured terminal-retention horizon: 90 days by default and never below 30 days, beyond GitHub Cloud's documented three-day redelivery window. Abandoned webhook payload rows compact only when the retained operator audit exactly matches event, payload digest, byte count, received, claimed, and failed timestamps, and failure. That retained audit permanently refuses the delivery ID after payload deletion, while item and byte capacity are released.

Managed check observations are monotonic by completion time. Older deliveries cannot override newer authority. Equal-time distinct check-run IDs, or contradictory authority for the same check-run ID, become a canonical ambiguous observation and fail closed. Migration 010 terminalizes only pre-010 pr_open or ci_green runs that depend on unverifiable legacy observations, emits an event and pending projection, then clears those observations. A new canonical attempt is required; no compatibility interpretation is provided.

A read-only recovery inspection lists only current ambiguous registrations, missed completions, failed projections, and failed signed webhook deliveries. Its action-specific digest binds status, failure, target/run identity, workflow correlation, and delivery payload digest plus timestamps without exposing the payload or a dispatch capability. Five actions require that exact state and a stable operation ID. Completion recovery applies the normal lifecycle and releases the external lease atomically. Delivery requeue preserves the original signed bytes; abandon preserves the failed-delivery evidence. A later recurrence needs a new inspection and operation.

claims.text: PostgreSQL is the single run authority, and every stage advances by exact version CAS. Physical content and webhook retention remain bounded and audit-bound. Source, base, head, check, or merge events invalidate dependent proof monotonically.

evidence.excerpt: The active and terminal states are finite; each stage row locks the run and advances exactly one expected status and version.
Main movement, head movement, close, and Merge Authority App merge observations have explicit ordered transitions.
Candidate publication requires all eight ordered exact stage digests with early stages at base and final stages at candidate head.

Configured terminal retention is bounded from 30 through 3,650 days with a 90-day default. Compaction releases raw allocation while preserving audit rows. An abandoned webhook row is deleted only when its retained operator audit matches payload identity, timestamps, and failure; admission then treats that audit as a permanent delivery tombstone.

Check observation CAS rejects older evidence and canonicalizes equal-time conflicts as ambiguous. The forward migration terminalizes affected active legacy runs before clearing unverifiable observations. Abandoned payload compaction retains an exact audit that admission uses as a tombstone.

No-overwrite publication returns exact creation receipts; same-issue replacement can reach canonical supersession while external execution stays leased; blocked admission cannot dispatch; snapshot and stage capacity is locked before writes; known failures delete only newly created unreferenced content.

blocks.text: Canonical v2 CI, review, human intent, protected intent, and managed intent identities bind one pull request to base SHA, head SHA, GitHub test-merge commit SHA, test-merge tree SHA, and policy SHA-256. Review adds the bounded subject digest. Human intent adds the current writer actor. Managed intent adds the exact managed evidence digest.

Each merge path acquires cloudx-main-merge-v1 with queued, non-cancelling repository-wide concurrency. The controller evaluates current state twice and rereads main and PR identity at the final actuation boundary. It then rechecks route-specific intent authority when applicable before one SHA-bound squash request, and it never retries. On the managed route, that same trusted controller calls the manager's live source authorization only after the final identity read and immediately before the sole merge request. A stale issue, approval, media byte, capability, or workflow identity therefore produces no merge request or main update. The result token and scoped Merge Authority App token coexist only inside this deterministic controller and are never exposed to model or candidate code. The controller then confirms the PR merge actor, main ref, squash commit parent, and resulting tree against the tested merge tree.

Candidate publication re-fetches the created or reused pull request before labels or provenance publication and requires its exact base SHA, head SHA, base ref, and head ref to match immutable candidate evidence. CI publication runs only for pull-request source runs. Managed automation creates an exact in-progress audit check, attempts immediate completion, and runs a separate always reconciliation job that locates the check by head, name, App ID, and external ID before completing it idempotently.

claims.text: Merge authority requires one canonical v2 base/head/test-merge/tree/policy identity, serialized live rereads, one SHA-bound squash request, and exact post-merge tree confirmation.

evidence.excerpt: Canonical v2 identities bind PR, base, head, ordered test-merge parents, test tree, and policy plus exact kind qualifiers.
The manager parses v2 CI/review checks and requires the same test-merge commit and tree before dispatching managed intent.

The controller performs repeated current-state reads, then the managed route consumes live source authorization inside the controller immediately before its sole SHA-bound squash request. It verifies Merge App actor, main ref, exact base parent, and tested tree after mutation.

All three merge jobs use cloudx-main-merge-v1 with queue max and no cancellation. Managed automation passes its manager credential and scoped Merge App token only to the exact merge controller; it has immediate and independent exact-check completion paths.

Publication verifies the created or reused PR's exact refs and SHAs before mutation; CI publisher excludes main-push runs; automation audit reconciliation matches exact head, name, App, and external identity.

blocks.text: The supported private deployment runs the manager, PostgreSQL, and a pinned Caddy TLS proxy. The operator dashboard remains loopback-only while signed webhooks and bearer-authenticated callbacks use the public HTTPS origin. Long-lived services have init reaping and explicit resource ceilings. Manager shutdown uses one 30-second global deadline within a 45-second container grace. PostgreSQL receives 60 seconds and is pinned to the immutable current 18.4 Bookworm image. Startup applies 12 bounded numbered migrations transactionally and validates prior migration digests. The manager image records the controller commit as its OCI revision. Initialize requires an exact empty Compose target. Backup, upgrade, and restore preserve co-consistent database, artifact, image, and deployment identities without a down-migration path.

Completion has two evidence classes. Local source, tests, images, Compose, migrations, and readiness can prove the deployable unit. Only a zero-blocker activation inspection plus live sequential logged-in model jobs and a disposable-repository run can prove runner authentication persistence, App identity, public webhook delivery, environment authorization, issue discussion projection, workflow isolation, and exact merge actuation.

claims.text: The manager migrates as one resource-bounded cleanly stopped control-plane unit whose PostgreSQL state, content-addressed volume, repository revision, immutable image ID and OCI revision, configuration, and secrets remain co-consistent.

evidence.excerpt: The supported topology has one manager, PostgreSQL, one state volume, explicit service ceilings and init reaping, one global shutdown deadline within Compose grace, a pre-mutation tooling capability gate, exact full stopped-manager recovery identity, checked same-major PostgreSQL minor updates, empty-target initialize and restore, and pending-service cleanup on failed final validation.
Schema changes are numbered and digest-checked while relational state references content-addressed bytes on the volume.

Tests reject edited migration history, unsupported Docker tooling before mutation, PostgreSQL major change or minor downgrade, unexpected inputs, missing content, startup partial failure, fatal shutdown deadline failure, populated initialize or restore targets, mismatched upgrade identity, repeated startup, image mismatch, failed container start, and failed post-start identity. The real PostgreSQL suite applies all 12 migrations across fresh and populated forward paths.
